name: Luxor
tagline: The site of ancient Thebes, genuinely described as the world's largest open-air museum, temples and royal tombs on both banks of the Nile.
highlight: Drifting silently over the Valley of the Kings in a hot air balloon at dawn, the whole west bank of temples and tombs spread out below in the first light.
shortDescription: The site of ancient Thebes, home to Karnak and Luxor temples, the Valley of the Kings, and a wealth of ancient sites often called the world's largest open-air museum.
metaDescription: A Luxor travel guide: Karnak Temple, the Valley of the Kings, hot air balloon rides, food and how to plan a visit to ancient Thebes.

intro: Luxor sits genuinely on the site of ancient Thebes, once the capital of Egypt's New Kingdom and often described as the world's largest open-air museum for the sheer density of temples and tombs packed into a single city.

Its east bank holds genuinely the living city and its two great temples, Karnak and Luxor, while the west bank, the traditional realm of the dead in ancient Egyptian belief, holds the Valley of the Kings and the mortuary temples surrounding it.
Most visitors genuinely spend a few days here, splitting time between the two banks and, for many, a dawn hot air balloon ride that has become one of Egypt's most iconic experiences in its own right.

whyVisit.intro: Luxor's case rests on genuinely being the single densest concentration of ancient Egyptian monuments anywhere in the country.

points.title: Karnak is genuinely the largest religious complex ever built
points.text: A vast temple complex constructed and expanded over nearly 2,000 years.

points.title: The Valley of the Kings is genuinely one of archaeology's great sites
points.text: The burial ground of pharaohs including Tutankhamun, hidden in a desert valley.

points.title: Luxor Temple is genuinely stunning after dark
points.text: Beautifully lit at night, offering a very different experience from a daytime visit.

points.title: A sunrise hot air balloon ride is genuinely unforgettable
points.text: Drifting silently over the west bank's temples and tombs as the sun comes up.

points.title: It's genuinely the natural start or end point for a Nile cruise
points.text: Most Luxor-Aswan cruises begin or end here.

attractionsIntro: Luxor's essential sights split genuinely between the living city's temples on the east bank and the royal tombs of the west.

attractions.name: Karnak Temple

image.file: File:Templo de Karnak, Luxor, Egipto, 2022-04-03, DD 144.jpg
image.alt: The vast temple complex of Karnak in Luxor

attractions.text: Genuinely the largest religious complex ever built, constructed and expanded by successive pharaohs over nearly 2,000 years.
attractions.tip: Genuinely allow at least half a day — the complex is far larger than a quick visit can properly cover.

attractions.name: Luxor Temple

image.file: File:Luxor Temple at night, Luxor, Egypt.jpg

attractions.text: Genuinely stunning after dark, beautifully lit colonnades and statues right in the heart of the modern city.
attractions.tip: Genuinely visit both during the day and after dark — the two experiences feel like different places entirely.

attractions.name: The Valley of the Kings

image.file: File:Thebes, Luxor, Egypt, Panoramic view of the Valley of the Kings.jpg
image.alt: The Valley of the Kings near Luxor

attractions.text: Genuinely the burial ground of Egypt's New Kingdom pharaohs, including Tutankhamun, hidden in a remote desert valley.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a limited number of tombs are open on rotation — check which are accessible before visiting.

attractions.name: The Temple of Hatshepsut

image.file: File:Templo funerario de Hatshepsut, Luxor, Egipto, 2022-04-03, DD 13.jpg
image.alt: The mortuary temple of Hatshepsut near Luxor

attractions.text: Genuinely a striking, unusually modern-looking mortuary temple built for one of ancient Egypt's few female pharaohs.
attractions.tip: Genuinely the temple's dramatic terraced design set against sheer cliffs makes it one of Luxor's most photogenic sites.

attractions.name: The Colossi of Memnon

image.alt: The Colossi of Memnon statues near Luxor

attractions.text: Genuinely two massive stone statues, all that remains of a mortuary temple that once stood behind them.
attractions.tip: Genuinely an easy, quick stop, often visited on the way to or from the Valley of the Kings.

attractions.name: Luxor at sunrise

image.file: File:Vista aérea de Luxor al amanecer, Egipto, 2022-04-03, DD 03.jpg
image.alt: Luxor and the Nile viewed from above at sunrise

attractions.text: Genuinely one of Egypt's most memorable sights, the whole west bank spread out below in the first golden light of day.
attractions.tip: Genuinely best experienced from a hot air balloon, though the view from a west bank hilltop is also striking.

attractions.name: Karnak's Great Hypostyle Hall

image.file: File:Templo de Karnak, Luxor, Egipto, 2022-04-03, DD 139.jpg
image.alt: The Great Hypostyle Hall at Karnak Temple

attractions.text: Genuinely one of the most awe-inspiring spaces in ancient architecture, a forest of massive columns towering overhead.
attractions.tip: Genuinely the columns' scale is best appreciated by standing directly beneath one and looking straight up.

thingsToDoIntro: Luxor genuinely rewards an early start, whether for the heat, the light, or a dawn balloon ride.

thingsToDo.title: Ride a hot air balloon at sunrise

image.alt: A hot air balloon flight over Luxor at sunrise

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely unforgettable way to see the west bank, drifting silently over temples and tombs as the sun rises.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book with a reputable operator, and expect a very early hotel pickup, often before 4am.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Karnak's columns

image.file: File:Templo de Karnak, Luxor, Egipto, 2022-04-03, DD 155.jpg

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely absorbing way to spend a morning, tracing nearly 2,000 years of ancient additions to a single complex.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely hire a guide here — Karnak's history and layout are hard to fully appreciate alone.

thingsToDo.title: Explore a tomb in the Valley of the Kings

image.file: File:Luxor Valley of the Kings R01.jpg
image.alt: Exploring a tomb in the Valley of the Kings

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely moving experience, descending into brightly painted burial chambers built for ancient pharaohs.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely Tutankhamun's tomb requires a separate ticket and is smaller, but genuinely worth it for its history.

thingsToDo.title: Visit the Temple of Hatshepsut

image.file: File:Templo funerario de Hatshepsut, Valle de las Reyes, Luxor, Egipto, 2022-04-03, DD 118.jpg
image.alt: The terraces of the Temple of Hatshepsut

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely striking stop, its dramatic terraced design set against sheer desert cliffs.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely combine with a Valley of the Kings visit, since both sit close together on the west bank.

thingsToDo.title: See Luxor Temple lit up at night

image.file: File:Luxor Temple at night, lights, Luxor, Egypt.jpg
image.alt: Luxor Temple's columns lit up at night

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely magical evening stop, the temple's columns and statues beautifully illuminated after dark.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a very different atmosphere from a daytime visit — worth doing both if time allows.

thingsToDo.title: Photograph the Colossi of Memnon

image.file: File:Colosos de Memnón, Luxor, Egipto, 2022-04-03, DD 132.jpg

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely quick, easy stop, two massive weathered statues standing alone in open farmland.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely early morning light works especially well for photos here.

foodIntro: Luxor's food genuinely reflects Upper Egypt's traditional staples, with fresh Nile fish a local highlight.

foods.name: Koshari

image.alt: Koshari, Egypt's national dish of rice, lentils and pasta

foods.text: A genuinely reliable classic, found throughout the city at every price point.

foods.name: Ful medames

image.alt: Ful medames, a traditional Egyptian fava bean breakfast

foods.text: A genuinely essential breakfast before an early temple visit or balloon ride.
foods.whereToTry: Breakfast stalls and cafés throughout Luxor.

foods.name: Fresh Nile fish
foods.text: Genuinely a local specialty, fish caught fresh from the Nile and grilled simply with local spices.

foods.name: Molokhia
foods.text: Genuinely a beloved home-style dish, a thick green soup found at traditional restaurants across the city.

foods.name: Taameya (Egyptian falafel)
foods.text: Genuinely Egypt's own fava bean version of falafel, found at street stalls throughout the city.

foods.name: Karkade (hibiscus tea)
foods.text: Genuinely a refreshing national drink, especially welcome in Luxor's dry heat.

accommodation.intro: Luxor genuinely offers accommodation on both riverbanks, with the east bank the more central, practical base.

areas.name: East bank (central Luxor)
areas.bestFor: Being genuinely central to Karnak, Luxor Temple and the corniche
areas.text: The most convenient base, with the widest choice of hotels and restaurants.

areas.name: West bank
areas.bestFor: A genuinely quieter stay closer to the Valley of the Kings
areas.text: Fewer options, but a short ferry ride from the east bank and closer to the tombs.

gettingThere.intro: Luxor is genuinely well connected by flight, train and Nile cruise boat from Cairo.

options.text: Genuinely the fastest option, taking about an hour and a half.
options.detail: Frequent daily flights make Luxor an easy addition to any Egypt itinerary.

options.text: Genuinely a budget-friendly, if slower, option with comfortable sleeper cabins.
options.detail: Saves a hotel night while covering the long distance from Cairo.

options.text: Genuinely the classic way to arrive, sailing north with stops at Edfu and Kom Ombo along the way.
options.detail: A multi-night journey combining transport with guided temple visits.

gettingAround.intro: Luxor is genuinely split by the Nile, with a ferry, taxi or organised tour needed to cover both banks.

options.text: Genuinely a cheap, quick way to cross between the east and west banks.
options.detail: Regular sailings run throughout the day from the central corniche.

options.text: Genuinely the standard way to reach the Valley of the Kings and other west bank sites.
options.detail: Widely available and often bundled as a half-day or full-day package.

options.mode: On foot on the east bank
options.text: Genuinely easy for reaching Luxor Temple and the corniche from central hotels.
options.detail: Karnak sits a bit further out, better reached by taxi.

bestTime.headline: October to April for the mildest temperatures, essential for outdoor sightseeing
bestTime.summary: Luxor's genuinely desert climate makes it one of Egypt's hottest destinations, with winter and shoulder season far more comfortable.

seasons.text: Genuinely the mildest, most comfortable temperatures for a full day of temple sightseeing.
Genuinely warm but manageable heat with thinner crowds than peak winter.
Genuinely dangerous heat, often exceeding 40°C, making extensive outdoor sightseeing genuinely risky.

bestTime.avoid: Extensive outdoor sightseeing during Luxor's summer — genuinely some of the hottest temperatures in Egypt.

days.evening: Luxor Temple lit up at night.

days.afternoon: The Temple of Hatshepsut and the Colossi of Memnon.
days.evening: Dinner back on the east bank.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Luxor visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book genuinely a hot air balloon ride ahead — it's one of Luxor's most popular activities.
Start genuinely early for the Valley of the Kings, both for the heat and the crowds.
Check genuinely which tombs are open on rotation before planning your Valley of the Kings visit.
Bring genuinely sun protection and water regardless of season — Luxor's heat is genuinely intense.
Hire genuinely a licensed guide at Karnak — its history and scale reward real context.
Visit Luxor Temple genuinely both during the day and after dark for two distinct experiences.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Luxor?
faq.a: Two to three days genuinely covers Karnak, Luxor Temple and the Valley of the Kings comfortably.

faq.q: Is the hot air balloon ride worth it?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it's widely considered one of Egypt's most memorable experiences, offering a unique view over the west bank's temples and tombs.

faq.q: How many tombs can you visit in the Valley of the Kings?
faq.a: A standard ticket genuinely covers three tombs from a rotating selection, with Tutankhamun's tomb requiring a separate additional ticket.
Genuinely being the site of ancient Thebes, often called the world's largest open-air museum for its density of temples and royal tombs.

faq.q: Is Luxor part of a Nile cruise?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — most Nile cruises between Luxor and Aswan begin or end here, making it a natural starting point.
Genuinely very hot in summer, often exceeding 40°C — winter and shoulder season are far more comfortable for sightseeing.
